title: Shockwave therapy
what: A machine sends sound pulses through the skin to the painful spot. This starts tissue healing and reduces pain.
why: For heel spurs and long-lasting pain in the tendons of the shoulder, elbow, knee, or Achilles tendon.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes; a course is several sessions, once a week
tell_doctor: A tumor or inflammation in the treatment area
If you recently had an injection in that spot

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: No special preparation is needed. You can eat as usual.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Wear comfortable clothes so the treatment area is easy to uncover.

bring: Scans and reports, if you had them
steps: The doctor finds the most painful spot
Gel is put on your skin
The tip of the device is pressed to your skin
The device starts tapping. The strength is set by how it feels to you
The session ends and the gel is wiped off
feel: Over the sore spot it can really hurt. Tell the doctor and they will lower the strength
after: You can go home and do your usual things right away
Redness, mild swelling, or pain for 1 to 2 days is normal
For a couple of days, do not put heavy strain on the treated area
Relief often comes slowly, a few weeks after the course

faq.a: It can be uncomfortable, especially over the sore spot. The strength is set so you can bear it.

faq.q: How many sessions do I need?
faq.a: Usually 3 to 6 sessions, once a week. Your doctor will tell you the exact course.

faq.q: Does shockwave remove a heel spur?
faq.a: The spur itself usually stays, but the pain often gets less. The main goal is to calm the inflammation in the tissue.
